Cranachan

Served at: Burns Night Supper

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 5 min

Cranachan is a traditional Scottish dessert often served at Burns Night Suppers, celebrating the life and poetry of Robert Burns. This creamy, fruity treat combines whipped cream, toasted oats, honey, and fresh raspberries, embodying the flavors of the Scottish countryside.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (90 g) rolled oats
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) honey, plus extra for drizzling
  • 1 cup (240 ml) heavy cream
  • 8 ounces (225 g) fresh raspberries
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) Scotch whisky (optional)
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Method

  1. Toast the rolled oats in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant. Remove from heat and let cool.
  2. In a mixing bowl, whip the heavy cream with vanilla extract until soft peaks form.
  3. Gently fold in the honey and Scotch whisky (if using) into the whipped cream.
  4. Reserve a handful of raspberries for garnish, then gently fold the remaining raspberries into the cream mixture, lightly crushing some to release their juice.
  5. Layer the cranachan in serving glasses or bowls by alternating toasted oats, cream mixture, and raspberries.
  6. Top with the reserved raspberries, a sprinkle of toasted oats, and a drizzle of honey before serving.

Tips

  • For a non-alcoholic version, omit the whisky and add a splash of raspberry juice or water.
  • Use fresh, ripe raspberries for the best flavor, or substitute with strawberries if raspberries are unavailable.
  • Prepare the toasted oats in advance and store in an airtight container to keep them crisp.
